ordered_diagnoses: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with cardiac and lung cancer history
salient_findings: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level elevated at 40 ng/L
ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3 on ECG
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
Denies chest pain at presentation
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG shows T-wave inversions in leads I, aVL, V4, V5, and V6
Echocardiogram shows preserved left ventricular systolic function
Echocardiogram shows no regional wall motion abnormalities
Coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

rejected.why: There is no mention of sarcoidosis in the patient's history or findings that would suggest this diagnosis.
